title: Implement wingfoil memory submit
description: As Jordan, deliver feature P1.6 (US-3-09). See user story map US-3-09 and BDD p1-memory/P1.6-memory-submit.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Submit a draft document for approval
When I run "wingfoil memory submit task-101"
Then the document frontmatter becomes "status: pending"
And the transition is recorded in git
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil memory approve
description: As Sam, deliver feature P1.7 (US-2-10). See user story map US-2-10 and BDD p1-memory/P1.7-memory-approve.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Approve a pending document with a reason
When I run "wingfoil memory approve task-101 --reason 'meets standards'"
Then the document transitions to the type's post-review approved state
And the git commit records the approver identity, timestamp, and reason "meets standards"
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil memory reject
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P1.8 (US-4-11). See user story map US-4-11 and BDD p1-memory/P1.8-memory-reject.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Reject a pending document with feedback
When I run "wingfoil memory reject task-101 --reason 'tests missing'"
Then the document frontmatter becomes "status: draft"
And the git commit records the rejecter identity, timestamp, and reason "tests missing"
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil memory deprecate
description: As Casey, deliver feature P1.9 (US-5-04). See user story map US-5-04 and BDD p1-memory/P1.9-memory-deprecate.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Deprecate an approved document
When I run "wingfoil memory deprecate decision-12 --reason 'superseded by decision-20'"
Then the document frontmatter becomes "status: deprecated"
And the file remains present in the repository
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil memory history
description: As Casey, deliver feature P1.10 (US-5-08). See user story map US-5-08 and BDD p1-memory/P1.10-memory-history.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: View the full audit trail of a document
When I run "wingfoil memory history decision-12"
Then the output lists 3 entries in chronological order
And each entry shows author, ISO-8601 timestamp, state change, and reason
And the query returns in under 1 second

title: Implement wingfoil directive create
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P3.1 (US-4-02). See user story map US-4-02 and BDD p3-directives/P3.1-directive-create.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Create a new custom directive
When I run "wingfoil directive create --name no-direct-db-access"
Then a directive file "no-direct-db-access" is created under ".wingfoil/directives/custom/"
And the change is committed to git
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil directive assign
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P3.2 (US-4-05). See user story map US-4-05 and BDD p3-directives/P3.2-directive-assign.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Assign a directive to a role
When I run "wingfoil directive assign --directive testing --role developer"
Then the role "developer" lists "testing" among its assigned directives
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil directive remove
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P3.3 (US-6-07). See user story map US-6-07 and BDD p3-directives/P3.3-directive-remove.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Remove an unreferenced custom directive
Given "legacy-rule" is not assigned to any role or workflow step
When I run "wingfoil directive remove legacy-rule"
Then the directive file is deleted
And the removal is committed to git
And the command exits with code 0

title: Implement wingfoil directives list
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P3.4 (US-4-04). See user story map US-4-04 and BDD p3-directives/P3.4-directives-list.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: List all directives with assignments
When I run "wingfoil directives list"
Then the output includes the 6 built-in directives and "no-direct-db-access"
And each directive shows its assigned roles (or "unassigned")

title: Implement Project Directives (custom + built-in)
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P3.5 (US-4-03). See user story map US-4-03 and BDD p3-directives/P3.5-project-directives.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Directive storage layout exists after init
When I inspect ".wingfoil/directives/"
Then it contains a "built-in/" and a "custom/" subfolder
And both are tracked by git

title: Implement Auto-Load Directives by Role
description: As Jordan, deliver feature P3.6 (US-3-06). See user story map US-3-06 and BDD p3-directives/P3.6-auto-load-by-role.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Directives auto-load at task execution
When an agent executes a task under the "developer" role
Then the agent context includes the "testing" and "code-quality" directives
And 100% of the role's assigned directives are present in the context

title: Implement Role-Based Directive Assignment
description: As Morgan, deliver feature P3.7 (US-4-06). See user story map US-4-06 and BDD p3-directives/P3.7-role-based-assignment.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Bind multiple directives to one role
When I assign "testing", "code-quality", and "security" to role "developer"
Then role "developer" lists exactly those 3 directives

title: Implement Built-in Directive Templates
description: As Alex, deliver feature P3.8 (US-0A-09). See user story map US-0A-09 and BDD p3-directives/P3.8-builtin-directive-templates.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Built-in templates are installed during init
When initialization completes
Then ".wingfoil/directives/built-in/" contains exactly 6 templates
And the set is: code-quality, testing, code-review, architecture, security, documentation

title: Implement MCP Prompts (role-based)
description: As Agents, deliver feature P5.2.2 (US-1-06). See user story map US-1-06 and BDD p5-interaction/P5.2.2-mcp-prompts.feature.
acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Auto-load role prompt at session start
When an agent session starts under the "developer" role
Then the MCP prompt for "developer" is returned
And it embeds the "testing" and "code-quality" directives
